user_prompt: What is the effect of an implantable gentamicin-collagen sponge placed in the sternotomy wound, compared with no topical antimicrobial, on superficial surgical site infection (SSI) in adults undergoing cardiac surgery?  The intervention is specifically a gentamicin-collagen sponge (or gentamicin-impregnated collagen implant) applied locally to the sternal wound during closure — not a general topical antimicrobial, antiseptic wash, or systemic antibiotic.  The single target outcome is SUPERFICIAL surgical site infection — not deep SSI, not mediastinitis, and not the combined/total SSI figure. Deep SSI is a separate, related analysis in this review using the same studies.  This is dichotomous (event/no-event) data — please pool it as a Risk Ratio (RR), using each trial's reported number of superficial SSI events and total randomized per arm.
